threads.body: These new span assertions use `hasAttributesSatisfying(...)`, which silently ignores any unexpected attributes on the span. The existing assertions in this same file consistently use `hasAttributesSatisfyingExactly(...)` (e.g. lines 156, 187, 340, 371), which fails when an unexpected attribute is present and therefore validates the full attribute set. Prefer the exact variant here (and for the other new `_OTHER`/client span assertions in `testUnknownService` and `testTripleUnknownService`) so the tests don't miss regressions; this requires enumerating the remaining attributes the spans carry (e.g. the network/peer-service attributes shown in the existing tests).

threads.body: [General] This treats every exception from `decode(Channel, InputStream)` as an unknown-service failure. That method can also fail for malformed streams, unsupported serialization, payload limits, argument deserialization, or callback decoding for registered services, so those failures will now emit misleading `_OTHER` server spans. Gate span creation on evidence that service/method resolution failed (or instrument a lookup-specific point), and cover a known-service decode error to prevent over-capture.

[General] This public, non-`.internal` type was previously abstract with an accessible no-arg constructor; making it `final` with only a private constructor is binary-incompatible with existing `DubboRequest` subclasses. Since `DubboTelemetryBuilder` exposes this type to custom extractors and span-name customizers, please retain the subclassable/AutoValue shape while adding the nullable unknown-request state, or explicitly handle this as a documented breaking API change.

[General] Any throwable from `getRequestHandler` currently creates an `_OTHER` span, but Dubbo’s unknown-route case is specifically the 404 `HttpStatusException`; failures after an invoker is resolved (for example descriptor or codec construction) are for a recognized method. Filter for Dubbo’s not-found outcome before creating the unknown-service span so unrelated Triple failures are not mislabeled.

[General] The PR description says this resolves #15690, whose reported failure is for ordinary grpc-java `ServerBuilder` servers, but this matcher only instruments Dubbo Triple’s `GrpcRequestHandlerMapping`. No grpc-java server instrumentation is changed, so the linked issue remains unresolved outside Dubbo Triple. Please either narrow the PR description/link or implement the grpc-java path before auto-closing that issue.

[Style] Move `HttpRequestAccess` to the nested-class section at the end of the utility class. Its current placement splits the static fields (`MAP_GETTER` from `HTTP_REQUEST_GETTER` and the dedup key), contrary to the class organization order in `docs/contributing/style-guide.md:61-70`.

The path and method written onto this synthetic invocation are never read back. Every getter in `DubboRpcAttributesGetter` returns early on `isUnknownService()` before touching `request.invocation()`, the remaining extractors only look at the addresses, and `InstrumenterUtil.startAndEnd` bypasses `Instrumenter.start` so the header getter never runs either. `parseFullMethodName(uri)` alone supplies everything that ends up on the span.

```suggestion
    RpcInvocation rpcInvocation = new RpcInvocation();
```

Applying this also lets you drop `parseServiceAndMethod` and the `@SuppressWarnings("deprecation")` on this method — both are only needed for the dead writes.

This puts a javaagent-only construction path into the published `opentelemetry-apache-dubbo-2.7` API, where it becomes something we have to keep supporting for library users who never have a use for it. Please keep the factory package-private and reach it from the agent through `internal.DubboInternalHelper`, using the same extractor-registration bridge this PR already adds for the server instrumenter.

The `satisfiesAnyOf` doesn't add anything here — any string containing the fully-qualified `...api.MiddleService` also contains `MiddleService`, so both branches collapse to `contains("MiddleService")` and the method half of `rpc.method_original` is never checked. The test controls both the interface and the invoked method, so it can just assert the exact value.

```suggestion
                                  equalTo(
                                      RPC_METHOD_ORIGINAL,
                                      "io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.apachedubbo.v2_7.api.MiddleService/$invoke"),
```

Same pattern at the two other `RPC_METHOD_ORIGINAL` assertions in this file.

threads.body: `rpc.method_original` is new public incubator API, but nothing in this module exercises it — the only coverage is indirectly through the Dubbo tests. Worth adding a case to `RpcAttributesExtractorTest` that returns a non-null `getRpcMethodOriginal()` and checks the attribute is emitted under stable semconv and absent otherwise.

Is it possible to add a test that covers this dedup?

An alt implementation could store the marker in a `VirtualField<RpcInvocation, Boolean>` rather than an attachment. On the server side attachments are populated from client-controlled wire metadata, so a caller could possibly send `_otel_unknown_svc_span` themselves and suppress the span this is meant to capture.

Convention here is `getClass().getName() + "$..."` — a class literal inside `transform()` causes unwanted class resolution in the agent classloader. Same in `DecodeableRpcInvocationInstrumentation` (line 40) and `GrpcRequestHandlerMappingInstrumentation` (line 37).

```suggestion
        getClass().getName() + "$GetInvokerAdvice");
```

Could you use `io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.api.internal.Timer` here instead of wall-clock millis? It captures the start instant up front and computes elapsed time with `System.nanoTime()`, so the span duration isn't skewed by clock adjustments. That's what the JMS/Kafka/Pulsar/RocketMQ receive advices do when they start and end a span after the fact: enter returns a `@Nullable Timer` (null when disabled), and exit passes `timer.startTime()` / `timer.now()` to `InstrumenterUtil.startAndEnd`. Same in `DecodeableRpcInvocationInstrumentation` and `GrpcRequestHandlerMappingInstrumentation`.

This can use the semconv constant directly instead of declaring a local key. `RpcIncubatingAttributes.RPC_METHOD_ORIGINAL` exists in the semconv version used here, and this file already static-imports `RPC_METHOD` and `RPC_SYSTEM_NAME` from that same class. Adding `import static io.opentelemetry.semconv.incubating.RpcIncubatingAttributes.RPC_METHOD_ORIGINAL;` lets you drop this declaration and the new `AttributeKey` import.
